en.title: Drinks and toasts
en.summary: Tea, coffee and beer, and the words used to raise a glass.

paragraphs: Drinks are an important part of social life in English-speaking countries. This lesson shows you what people drink, how to order in a pub and how to make a toast.

Tea is Britain's national drink, and many people drink several cups a day. Coffee is more common in the United States. In a pub people buy a round of drinks, which means that each person takes a turn paying. At a wedding dinner, a guest raises his glass.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen, please raise your glasses. To the happy couple!

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Cheers! May you have many happy years together.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: It's mine. What would you like?

paragraphs: **1. Toasts use the preposition to.** To + a person or thing means we drink in their honour. Cheers is a general toast and also a way of saying thank you or goodbye in Britain. See Introduction to Grammar: Prepositions and conjunctions.

blocks.html:
ToastMeaning
To the bride and groom!wish them well
To absent friends!remember those not present
Cheers!general toast
Good health!wish for health

paragraphs: **2. May expresses a wish.** In a toast, may + subject + verb is a formal wish. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
FormExample
May you + verbMay you have many happy years.
May + subject + verbMay the best team win.
Here's to + nounHere's to a good year!
Please + imperativePlease raise your glasses.

items: A cuppa means a cup of tea; a round is a set of drinks bought by one person.
A pint is about half a litre; a half is half a pint.
Bitter and lager are kinds of beer.
Soft drinks without alcohol are always available.

paragraphs: Drinking too much is not admired, and a person who does not drink alcohol can always order a soft drink or a tea. Designated drivers stay sober so that their friends can get home safely.
